summary: The note surveys how virtual reality is changing filmmaking, covering 360-degree cameras, non-linear scriptwriting, directing in the round, acting, editing, genre, audience participation and distribution. It cites specific people and VR works from 2023-2024 as examples. It closes by noting barriers to adoption such as cost, motion sickness and the need for headsets.
one_line: Overview of how virtual reality reshapes filmmaking, from cameras and scripts to acting, editing, distribution and adoption challenges.
key_facts: VR filmmaking creates cinematic experiences that surround viewers with an immersive 360-degree environment, making them participants rather than passive observers.
In December 2023, cinematographer Emily Jacobsen introduced the Oculix 3000, a camera that captures high-fidelity 360-degree footage with dynamic range rivaling traditional film cameras.
The Oculix 3000 integrates real-time stitching software that reduces the time and resources needed for VR post-production.
Roberto García wrote the award-winning VR experience "Whispers of the Ancients," released on February 10, 2024, using non-linear, flexible stories that accommodate viewers' freedom of gaze.
In VR "directing in the round," there is no "behind the camera" for crew or equipment to hide, so directors must consider every angle and may use VR pre-visualization software.
Actress Anna Liu, interviewed on October 5, 2023, called working on the VR adaptation of "Midsummer Night's Dream" "theater in the round on steroids."
Editor Michael Zhang guided audiences through "Orbit's Odyssey" (launched September 17, 2023) using only auditory and visual stimuli, including spatial audio and timed cues.
VR has notably affected horror and fantasy genres by heightening fear and wonder.
The documentary "Through Their Eyes" (released November 1, 2023) placed viewers in the lives of refugees from war-torn regions.
The Sundance New Frontier festival expanded its VR section considerably by January 2024.
VR platforms and app stores are growing as distribution spaces, letting users download stories at home.
Barriers to widespread VR adoption include production cost, motion sickness in some viewers, and the need for specialized headsets.
